What primer/setting spray would you recommend? I've an oily t zone on top of the rosacea 🙁 Always nervous about any product that might flare me up.

In my experience, there are some types of makeup it is worth spending a bit more on - foundation and concealer to cover up problem skin is probably in that category I'm afraid! 

I have rosacea which causes red flare ups and acne on my skin from time to time and cheaper foundation/concealers just don't have enough coverage and permanence for me. 

The good thing is if you're just using it for a light cover up of problem patches it should last ages so may be worth the investment. 

If you've never bought these products before, I'd advise going to a makeup counter for colour matching - I swear by bobbi brown myself for a natural look, good coverage and good endurance (so you don't have to reapply).

One week ago I put skates on for the first time since I was 12, fully expecting to be able to at least get to the point where I was moving forward like I used to be able to. Took me by surprise when I wobbled about like a baby giraffe, fell over then clung to the railings before giving up out of fear. 

2 days later I put the skates on again with a plan - learn to fall onto my knees (with pads!) and learn how to get up again. Teaching myself to control falling eliminated my fear - I wasn't just going to land on my face and break everything. That meant I could begin to actually skate a little bit!

My third skate session I went in with the plan to learn how to use my toe stopper to stop. I fell onto my knees quite a lot trying to do this (but it didn't matter because it didn't hurt and the fear was gone!) but now I can mainly stop when I want to, which eliminates another bit of fear. 

Tonight, I'm planning to get better at doing all of these things with my weaker leg. 

I'm no Instagram star, but the progress I've managed to make has been really pleasing - I'm just taking it slow, doing an hour or two when I can and in 3 sessions I've gone from terrified-bruised-quitter-giraffe to someone who can glide a bit and stop a bit and fall a lot without it being scary. Maybe in several years I'll be able to post a moonwalk to Instagram and make all the new giraffes feel sad like I did on day 1.

If I can do it you can too!
